concept.title: What this is, and what it is not
concept.shortdesc: An early demonstrator of discovering a service classification from real directory data, built on a pilot. It is a draft for people to review, not a published classification.

conbody.note: This is a draft built by software and language models. No person has reviewed, accepted or renamed any category. Names, definitions, groups and the links to needs are proposals. Identifiers change whenever the pipeline is re-run.

section.title: What it shows
section.p: It shows the approach in the guide running end to end on real data: service descriptions from several local directories were harvested, restated, grouped by meaning and named, and the result was tested against what people need. The three dimensions hold 115 service-type, 76 audience and 29 eligibility categories, each a concept page with its definition, its boundaries and its evidence.

ul.li: Not a release. No category is frozen, and no stable identifier exists yet.
Not reviewed. The review queue lists what a person must look at first: .

Not properly de-duplicated. The discovery ran ahead of the de-duplication step, using only a simple stand-in rule (it found 2 duplicate groups across directories), so sizes and stability are provisional.
Not a complete test. The needs-based test was judged by a model, and its pass marks are placeholders: .
Uneven in its sources. One directory (Shropshire) was harvested from an older interface because its newer one could not show every record; about one record in twelve there has less detail.
